"The EVENT LOG accumulates separately from the graph, and has its own prune: `rigger \
         reset --derived`. Each run's project-ingest pass records the project's derived index - \
         the code entities, inferred edges, design links, and doc concepts folded from your \
         sources - and a log written before that pass deduplicated across runs holds the WHOLE \
         index once per run, which is re-derivable duplication rather than history. `rigger reset \
         --derived` keeps, for each file, only the recordings of its LATEST generation - the \
         content the log last recorded for it - and of those the LATEST event per replay key, \
         deletes every superseded generation and re-recording, and compacts the file so \
         events.db shrinks on disk. Every other event survives byte-for-byte - lessons, \
         decisions, findings, gate verdicts, and the whole run history `rigger stats` and replay \
         read. The live graph a rebuild folds is unchanged: a newer generation of a file \
         retires every fact the one before it asserted and it does not, so the whole log \
         already folds to each file's latest generation; nothing reads a shed recording again \
         (a file that returns to an earlier content re-emits its batch); and the prune carries \
         a design fact's EARLIEST valid-time within its unbroken run of generations onto the \
         recording it keeps, so a design fact keeps the date it first became true rather than \
         being re-dated to whichever recording survived. WHAT IT CANNOT RECLAIM, because \
         this decides whether it is worth running at all: it never sheds the index itself. The latest generation of every file stays, so on \
         a log that holds each file once, at one recording per key, `rigger reset --derived` \
         deletes ZERO rows from it and reports so - that is the expected report on a clean log, \
         not a failure, and the derived index remains the bulk of the log by design because it \
         is what the graph is folded from. WHEN A DEDUPLICATED LOG STILL HAS SOMETHING TO SHED, \
         because a non-zero prune is otherwise read as a broken dedup: every edit to a file \
         records a new generation of its batch and leaves the one before it superseded, and a \
         file whose content has RETURNED to a generation the log had already recorded - a \
         revert, a branch switch, a checkout back - re-records that file's whole batch by \
         design, since a dedup that suppressed an already-recorded key would strand the graph \
         on the version the file has since moved past. A prune that sheds rows on such a log is \
         shedding exactly that, not covering for a defect; a log written BEFORE the dedup sheds \
         the whole accumulated pile instead. WHAT IT COSTS TO RUN: the compaction rewrites events.db in full and stages \
         a COMPLETE COPY of the log in SQLite's temporary directory while it does, so the free \
         space it needs is on whichever filesystem that resolves to rather than on the partition \
         holding .rigger/ - SQLITE_TMPDIR if you set it, else TMPDIR, else the first of /var/tmp, \
         /usr/tmp, /tmp that exists and is writable, which on a Linux box with TMPDIR unset means \
         /var/tmp and NOT /tmp. Set TMPDIR yourself if the default lands somewhere too small for \
         a second copy of your log. It rewrites only when the FILE is holding reclaimable free \
         pages, which is not the same as this run having deleted something: a prune with nothing \
         to shed from an already-compact log leaves the file exactly as it found it and reports \
         reclaiming zero, while a prune that sheds nothing from a log still holding free pages \
         reclaims them. That is what makes the re-run a real remedy - if the rewrite fails after \
         the deletes have committed, the command still reports what it removed and names the \
         failure, and because the deletes are durable and the space they freed is still free in \
         the file, re-running it is both safe and the way to reclaim that space. The two flags \
         COMPOSE \
         and each prunes its own accumulation: `rigger reset --runs --derived` sheds the dead-run \
         graph rows and the duplicated index in one pass. Both are one-shot maintenance you run \
         BETWEEN runs, never against a live one - and `--derived` ENFORCES that itself: a \
         compaction leaves revision gaps by design, and a writer whose cursor was built before it \
         ran could reissue a gap and reorder the log, so it refuses while a `rigger step` holds \
         its lock, a unit in the current run is not yet terminal, a spawn is in flight, or a \
         driver registration for this store is still live, naming what it found. `--force-live` \
         overrides the refusal for an operator certain no writer is using the store; it checks \
         nothing.\n"

"rigger keeps three stores under `.rigger/`, and only one of them holds anything \
             durable:\n"

"`rigger graph build` folds the project's source straight into `.rigger/graph.db` - \
             no run, no `RunStarted`, nothing but the code-ingest events the fold already emits. \
             It CREATES the store when the checkout is cold (`.rigger/` does not exist yet) and \
             REFRESHES an existing store incrementally: an unchanged file re-ingests nothing, and \
             it reuses the exact same walk-and-content-key ingest authority a live run uses, so a \
             standalone build and a run can never fold the same file under two different keys.\n"

"Never force a rebuild by deleting `.rigger/graph.db` (or `events.db`) and \
         re-running `rigger graph build` on the empty result. Deleting the log throws away \
         truth that no rebuild can get back, and deleting only the graph is unnecessary work \
         `rigger graph build` already does FOR you, incrementally, without erasing anything \
         first. If lookups are empty, just run `rigger graph build`; only reach for \
         rigger-reset-store if you specifically mean to prune, not rebuild.\n"

             walk of the whole tree.\n"

r#"__BEGIN__
# Check rigger's code-derived docs against a fresh render before THIS commit lands, so a
# commit that changes a documented code fact can only land carrying freshly rendered docs.
# SAFE to share: it reads and compares ONLY the two rendered outputs (never other working-tree
# files) and NEVER stages anything itself - staging is always the operator's own act. It acts
# ONLY where the repo already tracks those docs (inert in an operator project that does not
# carry them). A missing or failing `rigger` warns and lets the commit proceed (`rigger
# validate` / the CI drift check is the hard backstop for that case) - but once a render
# succeeds and DIFFERS from what is already staged, the commit is REFUSED rather than
# silently rewritten: a stale binary on PATH must never launder its own re-render into a
# commit over the operator's correctly staged content.
#
# BINARY SELECTION (spec 75): prefer a `rigger` BUILT FROM THIS TREE over whatever happens to
# sit first on PATH, so a worktree whose code legitimately changes a rendered fact renders with
# a binary that actually reflects that change instead of deadlocking against a stale PATH
# install. Candidate order, most authoritative first: the env-provided cargo target dir
# (release then debug), this working tree's own local target (release then debug), this
# worktree's own unit-derived scratch cargo-target - its unit is read from the worktree
# directory name, `rigger-wt-<unit>` (release then debug), the run's shared step-cache target
# (debug only - unit gates build the debug profile only), and finally PATH. SAFE-CLOSED: a
# wrong candidate can only ever convert a false refusal into a pass when its render genuinely
# matches what is already staged - never the reverse - so this can only make the hook MORE
# correct, never less.
git_common_dir=$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)
worktree_top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)
worktree_base=$(basename "$worktree_top" 2>/dev/null)
unit=
case "$worktree_base" in
    rigger-wt-*) unit="${worktree_base#rigger-wt-}" ;;
esac
# The relocated per-unit target (spec 89): a unit's build cache is the sibling
# `cargo-target-<unit>` of its worktree under `<cache home>/rigger/<encoded repo root>`,
# where the repo root is encoded byte by byte - alphanumerics and `-` kept, every other
# byte as `_xx` hex - exactly as the binary encodes it, so this shell derivation and the
# Rust one name the same directory.
encode_repo_path() {
    p="$1"; out=""
    while [ -n "$p" ]; do
        c=${p%"${p#?}"}; p=${p#?}
        case "$c" in
            [A-Za-z0-9-]) out="$out$c" ;;
            *) out="$out$(printf '_%02x' "'$c")" ;;
        esac
    done
    printf '%s' "$out"
}
unit_release=
unit_debug=
relocated_release=
relocated_debug=
shared_debug=
if [ -n "$git_common_dir" ]; then
    if [ -n "$unit" ]; then
        unit_release="$git_common_dir/../.rigger/tmp/cargo-target-$unit/release/rigger"
        unit_debug="$git_common_dir/../.rigger/tmp/cargo-target-$unit/debug/rigger"
        repo_root=$(cd "$git_common_dir/.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
        if [ -n "$repo_root" ]; then
            cache_root="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/rigger/$(encode_repo_path "$repo_root")"
            relocated_release="$cache_root/cargo-target-$unit/release/rigger"
            relocated_debug="$cache_root/cargo-target-$unit/debug/rigger"
        fi
    fi
    shared_debug="$git_common_dir/../.rigger/tmp/cargo-target/debug/rigger"
fi
rigger_bin=
for candidate in \
    "${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:+$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/rigger}" \
    "${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:+$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug/rigger}" \
    "./target/release/rigger" \
    "./target/debug/rigger" \
    "$relocated_release" \
    "$relocated_debug" \
    "$unit_release" \
    "$unit_debug" \
    "$shared_debug" \
; do
    if [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ -x "$candidate" ]; then
        rigger_bin="$candidate"
        break
    fi
done
if [ -z "$rigger_bin" ] && command -v rigger >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rigger_bin=$(command -v rigger)
fi
if [ -n "$rigger_bin" ]; then
    # Only check in a repo that ALREADY TRACKS these rendered docs (rigger's own self-hosting
    # repo). An operator project never carries them, so leave it untouched.
    tracked=
    untracked=
    for doc in "__SKILL__" "__HANDBOOK__"; do
        if git ls-files --error-unmatch -- "$doc" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            tracked="${tracked:+$tracked }$doc"
        else
            untracked=1
        fi
    done
    # Check ONLY when EVERY rendered output is already tracked (rigger's own self-hosting
    # repo). If any is untracked - an operator project, or a partial-tracking state - stay inert
    # so `rigger docs` never runs and never creates a stray untracked doc file the operator did
    # not ask for.
    if [ -z "$untracked" ] && [ -n "$tracked" ]; then
        if "$rigger_bin" docs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # `rigger docs` just wrote a fresh render into the working tree. Compare it against
            # what is ALREADY STAGED (the index) - never stage the fresh render itself. A doc
            # that differs is drifted: either the staged content is genuinely stale, or this
            # invocation's `rigger` is stale relative to the tree; the hook cannot tell which,
            # so it refuses rather than guessing.
            drifted=
            for doc in $tracked; do
                if [ -f "$doc" ] && ! git diff --quiet -- "$doc" 2>/dev/null; then
                    drifted="${drifted:+$drifted }$doc"
                fi
            done
            if [ -n "$drifted" ]; then
                rigger_prov=$("$rigger_bin" version 2>/dev/null)
                echo "rigger: pre-commit: refusing to commit - the committed docs have drifted from a fresh render: $drifted" 1>&2
                echo "rigger: pre-commit: rendering binary: $rigger_bin ($rigger_prov)" 1>&2
                echo 'rigger: pre-commit: nothing was staged. Fix by either re-rendering with the tree-built binary (rigger docs, then git add the result), or reinstalling rigger so PATH points at a binary built from this tree' 1>&2
                exit 1
            fi
        else
            echo 'rigger: pre-commit: rigger docs failed; committing without regenerated docs (rigger validate is the backstop)' 1>&2
        fi
    fi
else
    echo 'rigger: pre-commit: no rigger binary found (checked the tree build output and PATH); skipping docs regeneration (rigger validate is the backstop)' 1>&2
fi
# Best-effort on unavailability only (the drift check is the hard backstop for that case): a
# matching render (or a `rigger` that could not even attempt one) falls through to here and
# never blocks a commit. A DETECTED drift already `exit 1`'d above and never reaches this line.
true
__END__

"# Scaffolded by `rigger init`. A worked plan -> implement pipeline where the
\
# review is PER UNIT: each unit implements, three-tier-reviews ITSELF (lenses ->
\
# adversary -> adjudicator via defaults.review), and integrates in one lifecycle.
\
# Replace the gate commands with your own.
\

\
defaults:
  \
autonomy: auto_notify   # manual | auto_notify | silent
  \
grounder: symbols       # symbols (default; the structural symbol index) | grep | nop
  \
# The spawn-budget circuit-breaker: the hard cap on agent spawns one unattended
  \
# run may make. At the cap the breaker emits BudgetExhausted and aborts the run,
  \
# so a runaway can never spawn unboundedly. NON-ZERO on purpose - 0 = unlimited.
  \
budget: 60
  \
# The remediation depth: how many attempts a failed unit gets before it escalates
  \
# to a human. This is the REFINEMENT-depth knob, not a review-rigor one - raise it
  \
# to give a subtle unit room to CONVERGE under the full strict review instead of
  \
# escalating prematurely. It loosens the depth limit, never the review bar. Absent
  \
# falls back to 3 (the historical default); bounded by `budget` above.
  \
max_retries: 3
  \
# How many implement units build at once (spec 102, per-unit pipelining). Each
  \
# live unit owns its own build cache, and unbounded parallelism can fill disk on
  \
# a wide fan-out. 0 (the default) is unbounded, unchanged until you set this; 2
  \
# bounds the worst case to two live per-unit build caches at a time.
  \
max_parallel_units: 2
  \
# The three-tier review panel applied to EVERY implement unit. Declared once
  \
# here, inherited by the implement stage and every planner-proposed unit.
  \
review:
    \
lenses: [architecture-reviewer, sdet]   # tier 1: the expert lenses
    \
adversary: adversary           # tier 2: reviews the lenses and refutes them
    \
adjudicator: adjudicator   # tier 3: neutral judge; its verdict gates the unit
\

\
# The compilation-cache wrapper (spec 65): `auto` probes PATH for a known wrapper
\
# (sccache, ccache) and uses it when present, so a machine that already has one
\
# installed benefits with no further config; `off` disables the shared-cache
\
# layer entirely. See `rigger validate` for the resolved wrapper/cache dir/budget.
\
build:
  \
wrapper: auto
\

\
gates:                    # a reusable library of commands, referenced by name
  \
build: { run: "echo build ok; true", kind: core }
  \
test:  { run: "echo test ok; true",  kind: core }
  \
lint:  { run: "echo lint ok; true",  kind: elevated }
  \
# The check-in-stage mutation sweep (spec 91): runs ONCE, after every implement
  \
# unit has integrated - never per implementer round. For a Rust project, run the
  \
# sweep `rigger init` wrote beside this file: `run: "sh .rigger/gates/mutation.sh"`
  \
# (diff-scoped, in its own memory-bounded scope; its header explains each clause).
  \
# Declaring a gate under this exact id requires `cargo-mutants` on PATH (rigger
  \
# validate checks at run start).
  \
mutation: { run: "echo mutation ok; true", kind: core }
\
# The boundary gate: Clean Architecture made mechanical. Replace with your
  \
# project's own check that dependencies point inward and adapters are constructed
  \
# only in the composition root (see this crate's tests/boundary_audit.rs for the
  \
# worked example). A red boundary gate is non-negotiable: the adjudicator
  \
# rejects, never balances it against other evidence.
  \
boundary: { run: "echo boundary ok; true", kind: core }
\
# The audit gate: DRY and YAGNI as a red gate. Replace with your project's own
  \
# duplication and dead-code check; if it keeps a generated catalog, regenerate it
  \
# before asserting so a unit is never red on a stale catalog alone.
  \
audit: { run: "echo audit ok; true", kind: core }
\
# The red-before-green gate: TDD made mechanical. Replace with a check that a
  \
# unit's first source commit is preceded by (or carries) a test change (see this
  \
# crate's .rigger/gates/red-before-green.sh for the worked example).
  \
red-before-green: { run: "echo red-before-green ok; true", kind: core }
\

\
stages:
  \
# The conductor creates one baseline implement unit per acceptance criterion (the
  \
# deterministic decomposition); this planner REFINES that baseline via UnitProposed.
  \
# A produces stage decomposes the whole spec, so it has no single coverage criterion
  \
# - it grounds on the spec's acceptance criteria, not a `coverage` label.
  \
plan:
    \
agent: planner
    \
produces: dag           # refine the spec's unit DAG at runtime
\

  \
# The adversarial plan-critique gate: BEFORE any implementer spawns, the adversary +
  \
# adjudicator review the PROPOSED unit DAG for the cross-unit hazards per-unit review
  \
# cannot see: ambiguous mitigation ownership and open dispositions (a shared blast
  \
# radius is informational only - partition: by-blast-radius serializes it). A reject
  \
# feeds back to the
  \
# planner (bounded by max_retries); an approve releases the fan-out. Review-only (no
  \
# agent) - it critiques the plan, it does not implement.
  \
plan-critique:
    \
needs: [plan]
    \
adversary: adversary        # tier 2: reviews the DAG and refutes it
    \
adjudicator: adjudicator    # tier 3: its approve/reject gates the fan-out
\

  \
# Each unit implements, three-tier-reviews ITSELF (via defaults.review), and
  \
# integrates in one lifecycle. A reject or a gate failure feeds back into that
  \
# same unit's remediation loop; it does NOT integrate until approved + green.
  \
implement:
    \
needs: [plan-critique]
    \
agent: rust-engineer
    \
strategy: fan-out       # one worker per ready unit, in isolated worktrees
    \
partition: by-blast-radius
    \
gates: [build, audit, test, lint, boundary, red-before-green]  # red -> green enforced around the change
    \
on_pass: merge          # land + reindex + record, per unit, once reviewed
    \
coverage: "each unit is implemented, reviews itself, and integrates green"
\

  \
# 3. Check in ONCE, after every implement unit has integrated (spec 91): a
  \
# `needs` entry naming the fan-out `implement` TEMPLATE is satisfied exactly when
  \
# every unit it expanded into has integrated - never per implementer round, and
  \
# never before every unit has landed. Re-verifies the whole gate suite against
  \
# the merged tree, then sweeps mutants; one remediation round (max_retries: 2),
  \
# then integrate or escalate with the accounting already on record.
  \
checkin:
    \
needs: [implement]
    \
agent: rust-engineer
    \
max_retries: 2          # attempt bound: the sweep, one remediation round, the sweep again
    \
gates: [build, audit, test, lint, boundary, mutation]
    \
on_pass: merge
    \
coverage: "mutation efficacy of the whole spec diff"
"

rigger run [spec] [opts]    run the workflow (opts below)
  \
rigger step [--spec <path>]      advance the run one frontier via the replay driver
            \
[--base <ref>]        and print the newly parked spawn wave + a done flag
                              \
as JSON. --base (default origin/main) anchors a NEW run
                              \
branch; if it is unresolvable the branch is created off
                              \
HEAD. An existing run branch is reused, never reset.
                              \
--fresh begins a NEW run for the spec even if the latest
                              \
matches (pass on the first step to restart a wedged run);
                              \
--rebase-definition accepts a drifted definition and
                              \
continues, else a live-run step HALTS on definition drift
  \
rigger reported <id>        exit 0 iff spawn <id> already has a recorded result in
                              \
this project's run stream (else non-zero). A read-only check
                              \
of whether a spawn reported yet; the death courier records
                              \
atomically instead via `rigger result --if-absent`
  \
rigger prompt <id>          print the parked spawn's full prompt (persona + task).
                              \
The step wave is a slim manifest; each worker fetches its
                              \
own prompt from the log by spawn id (spawn-by-reference)
  \
rigger scratch <id>         print spawn <id>'s own rigger-assigned scratch container
                              \
(the exact dir the per-spawn reclaim reaps at its terminus);
                              \
a worker points agent-created scratch and manual
                              \
CARGO_TARGET_DIR there instead of an unbucketed literal
  \
rigger workflow [spec]      turn-key: launch the per-project Node driver, which
                              \
spawns `rigger serve`, runs each agent via the Agent
                              \
SDK, and drives the loop (one command; run `rigger
                              \
setup` first - it provisions the driver in .rigger/shim/)
  \
rigger serve [opts]         run as an MCP server the driver connects to
  \
rigger graph --around <id>  print the context subgraph around a node
  \
rigger graph --show <entity> print an entity's definition site + line-numbered body
                              \
(the text half of lookup; resolves a full id or a bare name)
  \
rigger graph build          fold the project's source into the graph from a cold
                              \
checkout (no run required)
  \
rigger graph communities    derive the code lens's coupling communities offline and
                              \
[--resolution <r>]          record them as events (deterministic; default r=1.0)
  \
rigger graph concepts       derive the concepts lens's intent-layer grouping offline
                              \
[--resolution <r>]          and record them as events (deterministic; default r=1.0)
  \
rigger stats                print the run's operator metrics: first-pass yield,
                              \
per-gate remediation counts, escalation rate, and
                              \
review approve/reject counts. --canary reports the
                              \
latest canary run's judge-the-judges recall scorecard
  \
rigger canary               run the review panel against the seeded-defect corpus
            \
[--corpus <dir>]         (default ./canaries) and score per-tier catch rate,
                              \
adjudicator correctness, and verdict stability under
                              \
finding-order shuffle, into the project's canary stream
                              \
(read back with `rigger stats --canary`)
            \
[--jobs <n>]              caps the total concurrent review-panel spawns
                              \
across sharded items and each item's lens fan-out
                              \
together (default: the crate's default worker
                              \
width, floored at 2)
            \
[--model <tier>=<id>]    pins a tier's (lens/adversary/adjudicator)
                              \
model for this run only, repeatable; the scorecard
                              \
header prints its resolved id
  \
rigger playbooks --rebuild  reconstruct the distilled playbook pool under
                              \
.rigger/playbooks/ from the recorded LessonLearned
                              \
stream: deduplicated, trigger-scoped agent-files the
                              \
lessons injector ranks by blast-radius relevance (a
                              \
rebuildable projection of the log, never hand-edited)
  \
rigger replay <run|latest>  re-drive a completed run's recorded trajectory under a
            \
--against <rev>          candidate config (workflow + prompts at git <rev>) in an
                              \
isolated scratch namespace, and print the stats diff
                              \
vs the recorded baseline. Never writes the real run
                              \
stream - past runs become a regression corpus for a
                              \
config edit ("did that change regress first-pass yield?")
  \
rigger status [--json|--line] present the live per-agent view of the current run: for
                              \
each in-flight agent, what it is doing (latest progress),
                              \
its heartbeat age, and how long since its last store event
                              \
(the blackout). --json prints the shim/dash machine shape;
                              \
--line prints only the one-line statusline (the same line
                              \
`rigger setup` registers as the editor's status bar)
  \
rigger dash [--port <n>]    serve the read-only observability page on 127.0.0.1
                              \
(default port 7420) with live past/present/future views;
                              \
--export <path> writes the equivalent static snapshot
  \
rigger watch [--interval <s>] the driver-independent watchdog: polls the store,
            \
[--once]                  process table, and status for the five rigger-watch-a-run
                              \
signals (escalated blockers, heartbeat staleness, dash
                              \
liveness, reject-recurrence trend, frontier progress) plus
                              \
store integrity, printing one line per anomaly naming
                              \
signal, subject, and response skill. --once prints standing
                              \
anomalies and exits (cron/CI); default streams (poll every
                              \
180s, dedup'd) and never talks to the driver - it works
                              \
with the driver dead
  \
rigger ground <query> [k]   print up to k (default 8) repo references the project's
                              \
configured grounder finds for <query>, as `file:line: text`
  \
rigger reindex <file>...    incrementally re-index the named files in the project's
                              \
persisted grounding index (the grounder's reindex), so a
                              \
later `rigger ground` reflects just-landed changes
  \
rigger symbols-index [dir]  build + persist the structural symbol index over [dir]
                              \
(default .) and print its path + file count - the fresh-
                              \
process determinism harness for the symbols grounder (spec 15)
  \
rigger emit <type> <json>   append {{type, data:<json>}} to the event store and fold
                              \
it into the context graph (the CLI form of rigger_emit)
  \
rigger progress <id> <act>  record one live progress line for spawn <id> to the
                              \
separate .rigger/progress.db (never the run stream), so an
                              \
observer can see what a working agent is doing between
                              \
milestones - `rigger status` and the dash present it
  \
rigger result <id> [out]    record a parked spawn's outcome to the run log so the next
                              \
step advances past it: <out> (or stdin) is the agent's output
                              \
(with --error, its failure message); --if-absent records only
                              \
if the id has no result; --meta <json> adds bookkeeping
  \
rigger peers [file ...]     print peer decisions, lessons, and findings from the
                              \
context graph, scoped to the given files (the CLI form of
                              \
rigger_peers)
  \
rigger reset --runs         drop every superseded / dead run's decisions and
                              \
findings from the context graph, keeping every lesson and
                              \
the active run's own decisions/findings. Sheds dead-run
                              \
grounding noise without wiping the store: it deletes no
                              \
event. reset itself does write the log once, on a store
                              \
still under the legacy basename namespace: the one-time
                              \
identity migration renames those streams and records one
                              \
DecisionMade before either mode prunes. When no driver is
                              \
alive, it also closes the current run's units whose branch
                              \
work is landed on rigger-run, appending the UnitIntegrated
                              \
a hand landing never recorded
  \
rigger reset --derived      compact the EVENT LOG: keep only each file's latest
                              \
generation of the derived index, at the latest event per
                              \
replay key, delete the superseded generations and
                              \
re-recordings, and vacuum so the file shrinks on disk.
                              \
Every other event survives. Sheds what edits and the
                              \
pre-dedup ingest accreted;
                              \
composes with --runs (each prunes its own accumulation).
                              \
Refuses while run machinery looks live (a held step
                              \
lock, a non-terminal unit, an in-flight spawn, or a live
                              \
driver registration), naming what is live: compaction
                              \
leaves revision gaps by design, and a stale writer can
                              \
reissue one and reorder the log - the corruption this
                              \
guard exists to prevent. --force-live skips the check
                              \
entirely and checks nothing: pass it only once you are
                              \
certain no writer is using this store, since forcing
                              \
past a genuinely live writer is exactly that corruption
  \
rigger reset --build-cache  reclaim the SHARED gate build cache (a pure cache,
                              \
always safe to cold-rebuild) under the scratch root.
                              \
Composes freely with --runs/--derived (each sheds its
                              \
own accumulation); reports the exact bytes reclaimed,
                              \
or 0 when there was nothing to reclaim. Refuses loudly
                              \
- never waiting - while a rigger-launched build still
                              \
holds the cache's guard lock; retry once it is idle
  \
rigger reset --scratch-orphans
                              \
reclaim every cache-home scratch root (under
                              \
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/rigger, else ~/.cache/rigger) whose repo
                              \
no longer exists: a root keyed on a deleted checkout or a
                              \
test fixture's tempdir has no owner left to reclaim it.
                              \
Rigger does this itself whenever it creates a default-
                              \
placed root; this is the explicit on-demand form. Reports
                              \
the number of roots reclaimed; composes with the others
  \
rigger validate             load and validate the workflow + agents
  \
rigger init                 set up a project: scaffold .rigger/ (workflow.yml +
                              \
an agents/ folder) and install the Claude Code
                              \
SessionStart hook (it runs `rigger prime`)
  \
rigger setup                full setup: everything `init` does, PLUS install the
                              \
native /rigger Claude Code workflow (.claude/workflows/
                              \
rigger.js) and provision the JS driver (.rigger/shim/ +
                              \
npm install). After it: run `/rigger <spec>` in Claude
                              \
Code (primary), or `rigger workflow` as a fallback
  \
rigger docs                 render the code-derived docs (every registry skill and
                              \
handbook page) into their committed paths
  \
rigger prime [<spec>]       print recent decisions (what the hook runs); given a spec
                              \
path, also names `rigger validate <spec>` (the pre-launch
                              \
spec lint) as a next step
  \
rigger instructions         print the instructions every spawned agent is held to:
                              \
the built-in law and working discipline, then each
                              \
operator file in .rigger/instructions/ (filename
                              \
order)
  \
rigger version              print the crate version and the build-provenance id
                              \
(a git commit/describe embedded at build time) so an
                              \
agent can identify the exact binary. Also `--version`

                                   \

halting. The explicit mid-campaign-edit escape (a live

        touching the largest raw line count anywhere in this plan.\n\
        6. Tier 6 - remaining catalog sweep: the {remaining} src-touching clusters section 2 \
